artworks.title: Haemon Discovering the Body of Antigone
artworks.description: Fuseli's gray-wash drawing (Huntington Library) freezes the Sophoclean catastrophe that defines Haemon: Creon's son finds Antigone hanged in her tomb and will turn the sword on himself. The British-Swiss Romantic stages the fiancé not as a debating prince but as a body stricken by sight — the visual counterpart to Antigone's last episode. Few images name Haemon so squarely; this one makes him the discoverer of the tragedy his father wrote.

films.title: Antigone
films.description: Irene Papas' Antigone buries Polynices against Creon; Haemon stands with her against his father — Sophocles filmed in Greece, the fiancé who chooses the tomb over the throne.

music.title: Antigone
music.description: Honegger's opera after Cocteau keeps Haemon in Sophocles' fatal geometry — the son who warns Creon and dies beside Antigone, set in stark modern harmony.

popCulture.title: Antigone
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' tragedy makes Haemon Creon's son and Antigone's betrothed — the voice of the city who fails to sway his father and dies by his own hand in her tomb.

popCulture.title: Antigone
popCulture.creator: Jean Anouilh
popCulture.description: Anouilh's Occupation-era rewrite keeps Haemon as the fiancé who offers escape and is refused — the Theban prince rewritten for a century that heard Creon as tyranny.
